transcript.text: bosch washer FD 9409 not draining. ive cleaned the filter already. what part do i need?

I cannot tell you which part to buy yet because 'not draining' after cleaning the filter usually points to one of two very different issues: either something is blocking the hose further down (which needs clearing, not replacing), or the drain pump motor itself has failed. To distinguish between these, please run a Drain or Spin programme and listen carefully at the bottom front of the machine. Does it hum/buzz as if trying to work, or is it silent? This tells us whether the pump is receiving power but blocked, or if it's dead.
it hums but the water doesn't go anywhere, with a bit of a rattle. no burning smell. so is it the pump then?

The humming with a rattle suggests something is caught in the pump impeller rather than the motor itself failing. Since cleaning the filter didn't solve it, please unplug the machine and remove the filter again to check if there's an object stuck in the small plastic fan blades (impeller) behind it. If you find debris, clear it and test a drain cycle; if the impeller is free but it still won't drain, the pump motor itself has likely failed.
ok did that. filter was just a bit of fluff, nothing big. impeller turns but feels a bit stiff and gritty in places. E18 showed up on the display too. so is it the pump?

[Heading: Likely cause: drain pump]
Yes, the stiff and gritty impeller suggests that the drain pump is failing. The E18 error happens because the machine cannot empty fast enough due to this internal wear or blockage. Since cleaning the filter did not fix it, you will need to replace the entire drain pump unit; a worn impeller usually means the motor bearings are also wearing out and won't last long if only the vanes were changed. I cannot provide specific part numbers for your model, but you can find the correct replacement on the manufacturer's official spares site or through an authorised engineer.
